title: Should You Buy an Appliance Warranty? What the Data Says
summary: An appliance retailer argues most appliance warranties fail due to tech shortages and profit incentives, but says its own service-backed plan and a few failure-prone appliance types are worth covering.

assertions.quote: There just aren't enough skilled techs.

verdicts.note: A real skilled-trades shortage exists, but claim denials and exclusions, not technician scarcity, are the better-documented reason warranties disappoint buyers.

assertions.quote: warranty companies subcontractor was ever the cheapest, you often don't get the right person for the job

verdicts.note: Warranty administrators do route jobs to low-bid subcontractors in some cases, but quality varies and this isn't quantified beyond anecdote.

assertions.quote: manufacturers will always prioritize new shipments over repairs

verdicts.note: Supply prioritization toward new units over service parts does occur during shortages, but 'always' prioritizing overstates a variable practice.

assertions.quote: a real repair on a Pro Range could cost $600 or more. They can afford that, say, delay, deny
If the store selling you the warranty doesn't have its own service department, you're basically buying a promise they can't keep.

verdicts.note: Self-funded, in-house-serviced warranties generally have fewer middlemen than reinsured third-party contracts, but this is one of several factors affecting claims experience, not a guarantee.

assertions.quote: The only time an extended warranty makes sense is if the storage is real accountability, their own technicians, their own trucks

verdicts.note: In-house service likely reduces subcontractor friction, but no independent data isolates this as the decisive factor in whether a warranty pays out fairly.

assertions.quote: Either because they break more often or because repair is expensive when they do.
If you don't use your warranty, you get 50% back as a credit.

verdicts.note: This is the seller's own specific policy, unverified independently, and such guarantees are frequently undercut industry-wide by friction in the credit or refund process.
